checks.title: Mass: released = held + carried out
checks.registered: 2026-09-29, before the transport family's first run
checks.measure: |change in the pollutant the river holds - dt (release + what crosses the edges)| over the mass released in the step, every step, worst arm
checks.why: the explicit finite-volume step moves mass face by face, what leaves one cell entering the next, so the full domain closes to the round-off of summing the field; the decomposed arm is the same step to round-off (the next check). 1e-9 leaves about four orders above that round-off

checks.title: Concentration agrees with the full domain
checks.registered: 2026-09-29, before the transport family's first run
checks.measure: max |c_decomposed - c_full| over the full domain's largest concentration, at the last step
checks.why: one explicit step on a window's cells is the full-domain step on those cells, so the arms differ only in the order of floating-point additions (the cut faces' rows, and the blend in the overlap): about one unit in the last place per step, which the monotone step never amplifies -- a few 1e-13 after a few thousand steps
checks.detail: max |dc| = 6.66e-16 mg/L against a peak of 1.552 mg/L

checks.title: Threaded equals serial, bit for bit
checks.registered: 2026-09-29, before the transport family's first run
checks.measure: np.array_equal on the concentration after every step
checks.why: each window's step reads only the previous step's field, and the blend adds the windows in their order, so the order the threads finish in cannot change a bit

checks.title: The river's flow is continuous, cell by cell
checks.registered: 2026-09-30, before the forked river's first run (demo-finish-plan section 2.4)
checks.measure: the largest |sum of a cell's flows| over the river's discharge (flow.py's residual), for a drawn river's solved flow
checks.why: the potential flow is one sparse direct solve, and each cell's flows are its own potential's differences, so they sum to the solve's round-off; a fork adds outlets, not arithmetic. River-bend measured 1.4e-14
checks.detail: largest |sum of a cell's flows| = 1.79e-14 of the discharge

notes: One explicit step of 1.7 s per macro-step, one exchange, no iteration: the stability limit here is 1.895 s (min h dx^2 / A_ii over the cells). Each window takes the full-domain step on its own cells, so the decomposed river is the full-domain river to round-off.

The river is drawn, so its flow is solved: the potential flow from its inlets to its outlets (atlas/workbench/flow.py), carrying the discharge per metre of the inlets' width. No water crosses a bank. It is a potential flow: it has no viscosity and turns corners without separating.

Reach shallow-fast: depth 1.25 m, so the water runs at 0.502 m/s on average; mixing 0.5 m^2/s; cell Peclet number u dx / D = 5.02, so what runs upstream across a face is 1/(1 + Pe) = 0.17 of what runs down. Upwinding adds 1.04 m^2/s of mixing along the flow.

The river leaves by 2 outlets: outlet B3 (outline:2) takes 50.0% of the water and 54.0% of the pollutant leaving (5.397 g/s); outlet B6 (outline:5) takes 50.0% of the water and 46.0% of the pollutant leaving (4.603 g/s). A potential flow splits by the channels' shapes alone, which is a stated guess, as the inlet on the left is.

layout.how: along the river's own flow, from its inlet to its outlets: the shape branches, so a band across two branches is two windows
